Dementia is a progressive, incurable condition that affects a person's memory, thinking and behaviour. It is estimated that there are 820,000 people with dementia in the UK and that this number will increase to over one million by 2025 (Alzheimer's Society, 2014). The majority of people with dementia will die in an acute hospital setting, and the majority of these deaths will be preceded by the withdrawal or withholding of life-sustaining treatment (LST) (Hockley _et al._, 2005). However, the views of people with dementia and their carers about end-of-life care are not always taken into account when decisions about LST are made (Hockley _et al._, 2005; Murtagh _et al._, 2014).
